clue.text: Apprentice that reveals lack of grip?

blocks.note: a lack of something means there is none of it
a vice is a bench tool that grips work tightly

explanation.surface: A trainee gives themselves away with a feeble handshake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'lack of grip' is to be read literally in pieces: NO plus VICE, the clamping tool (spelt 'vise' in American English).
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a beginner who is still learning a trade or skill.

clue.text: Arrest old boys and rich influential people

blocks.note: to nab is informal for to catch or arrest
OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, so two of them are OBS

explanation.surface: A call to lock up the old-school-tie brigade and the wealthy elite together.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school, abbreviated OB; the plural OBS is common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabob originally meant a governor in Mughal India, later any person of great wealth and power.

clue.text: Shot cavalier infected by Latin disease

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or broken, so the letters come out in a new order
whatever is infected has something get inside it, so one piece takes another within

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A dashing gentleman, done for, has caught some illness with a Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a gunshot wound but means ruined; the cavalier's letters are scrambled and the single L slipped in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Varicella is the medical term for chickenpox, a contagious viral illness.

clue.text: Obscure sort of clock light is an escape from reality

blocks.note: to cloud something is to obscure it
a cuckoo clock has a bird that pops out on the hour
to light on something is to land or settle on it

explanation.surface: Some murky glow from a clock seems to offer a way out of the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun or adjective but is the verb, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an imaginary realm of fantasy where impractical dreamers live, taken from Aristophanes' play The Birds.

clue.text: This might have made woman something to eat

blocks.note: first meaning: in Genesis, Eve was formed from a rib Adam could do without
second meaning: a cut of pork ribs with most of the meat trimmed off

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading of the Bible story in which God takes a rib from Adam to make Eve; a rib he could spare.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of pork from the ribcage is served as food, often barbecued, so it is literally something to eat.

clue.text: Penny’s on edge, being prudish

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Penny is jumpy and nervous because she is rather straitlaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; 'on edge' is read literally, the coin placed on top of the edge in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prim is stiffly proper and easily shocked, the same disposition as a prude.

clue.text: Very clever person notes it’s cricket to be played

indicators.note: something played is performed or worked through freely, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A genius records that the game about to start is cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's cricket' is also an old British phrase for fair play, which hides that the words are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a brilliant thinker, as in 'it doesn't take a rocket scientist'.

clue.text: Turns over parts in play to be broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the sound matters and not the spelling

blocks.note: the parts in a play are its roles

explanation.surface: Someone hands over sections of a drama that is going to be put on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns over' suggests handing something across; here it means rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball or a sleeper that rolls is rotating over and over, the same motion as turning over.

clue.text: Military quarters forbid instruments of torture

blocks.note: to bar is to forbid
the rack stretched victims to extract confessions

explanation.surface: An army camp bans the use of torture devices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military quarters' is read as one phrase; the wordplay is simply a verb followed by a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings where soldiers are housed, their quarters on a base.

clue.text: Old burial site featuring in pub argument?

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: An ancient grave gets mentioned during a heated pub dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'pub argument' is to be read as two words placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a prehistoric earth mound raised over graves, common in the English countryside.

clue.text: Letter like ‘O’

blocks.note: first meaning: a printed letter or notice sent to many people
second meaning: round in shape, as the letter O is

explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears to say O is a letter; 'Letter' is in fact a noun for a mass mailing and 'like O' an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailshot sent to many recipients is a noun sense, and ring-shaped is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Dressed in thong, zip to the USA

indicators.note: dressing a shop window or a salad means arranging it, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wearing only a thong, zipped up, is off to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' looks like a fastener; in American usage it means zero, as in a score of 'zip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say 'zip' informally for zero or none at all, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Stage set to see fall by defender

blocks.note: a back is a defending player in football or rugby
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A match is arranged so we can watch a defender take a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage set' reads as 'ready' but is a theatre noun; 'by' puts the fall beside the defender, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is the painted cloth hung at the rear of a theatre stage as scenery.

clue.text: Paid companion — his age is variable

indicators.note: whatever is variable can change its form, so the letters are shifted about

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hired escort's age changes depending on who's asking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' makes the companion sound male, but the word is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained in the arts and hired to entertain male guests.

clue.text: A requirement to include one’s flavouring

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a need is a requirement
one is I, and 'one's' is read as I'S

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a recipe must contain a certain seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive but is I (one) plus S; it goes inside after the first letter of the requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed, the seed of the anise plant, is used to give a liquorice taste to sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Victim as result of ‘Comedy Store’?

blocks.note: the result of comedy is people laughing
stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: Someone falls prey to a performer at the Comedy Store, a famous London stand-up club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club's name must be split: what comedy produces, then a synonym for store.
explanation.definitionFit: A laughing stock is a person everyone mocks, the butt or target of ridicule.

clue.text: Pig-headed and old, at best in being treated

indicators.note: material being treated is processed and altered, so the letters are changed round

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn elderly patient is at their finest while under medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being treated' suggests medical care but signals that the three short words are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone stubborn who refuses to change their mind.

clue.text: Set out to impound consignment — French delicacy

indicators.note: out can mean awry or disordered, so the letters are put in a different order
to impound is to lock something up, so one piece is shut inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a cargo is a consignment of goods

explanation.surface: Customs officers set out to seize a shipment of fine French food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as 'intended', but 'Set' is fodder and 'out' its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French culinary word for a snail, eaten cooked in garlic butter as a speciality.

clue.text: Relish errors by a person following mild punishment

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the pieces before this word are placed later in the answer

blocks.note: a smack is a light slap given as punishment
one is a person, as in 'one must'
slips are small errors

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys the mistakes a person makes after being given a light smack.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: errors come after the person, who comes after the punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To smack your lips is to show keen anticipation or enjoyment, an idiom for relish used as a verb.

clue.text: Elite religious body infiltrated by the Spanish

indicators.note: whatever is infiltrated has an intruder slip inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a sect is a religious group
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An exclusive religious order has been penetrated by Spanish agents.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish article goes in after the first letter of the religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words, used as adjectives, describe a small, exclusive group of the best.

clue.text: Part of play about fighting

blocks.note: Act I, the first act, is a part of a play
on means about, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: A section of a drama concerns combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The part of the play is ACT I, the Roman numeral supplying the letter I; 'about' simply means ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who see action are engaged in combat, so the words are synonyms in a military sense.

clue.text: Coach and team’s leader in heavy defeat, having been set up

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the first letter is kept
one thing in another sits inside it
in a down answer, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the order is flipped

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
the opening letter of the team

explanation.surface: The coach and the captain suffered a thrashing after being framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reads as framed, but in a down clue it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach and a tutor are both private teachers who give individual instruction.

clue.text: Neat changes in wordless performance one should see in the intervening period

indicators.note: whatever changes takes a new form, so the letters shift order
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: mime is acting without speech
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy costume changes in a silent show are what you watch between the main events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like praise for the changes; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the time between two events, as in 'in the meantime'.

clue.text: Punch that makes one black and blue

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A punch leaves someone bruised black and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'black and blue' means bruised, but here each colour gives letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch is a hard hit with a fist, and a blow is any forceful stroke.

clue.text: Understand restaurant booking is achievable

blocks.note: to get something is to understand it
at a restaurant you book a table

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a reservation at a restaurant can be had after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understand' looks like the definition, but it is the start of the wordplay; the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: What is obtainable or within reach can be got, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Fodder is turned and left to mature

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Farm feed is turned over and left to ripen, as happens in a silo.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little word 'is' is turned; 'left' and 'to mature' follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is grass or other green crops stored and fermented to feed livestock in winter.

clue.text: Reject drink after performance on stage

blocks.note: a turn is a short act in a variety show
to down a drink is to swallow it in one

explanation.surface: An actor refuses a drink offered after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the drink second; 'Reject drink' misleads as refusing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to decline or refuse it, a phrasal verb equal to reject.

clue.text: Witness‘s source of tension during a trial

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter is wanted
during places one event within the span of another, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a trial is a test
the opening letter of tension

explanation.surface: A witness in a court case is the cause of strain while the trial goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witness' and 'trial' paint a courtroom, but 'trial' here just means a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to sign and confirm it, which is exactly what attesting does.
